verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, right before the great war. Arjuna is paralyzed by doubt, and Krishna is telling him to act. Krishna says that on this path of action, no sincere effort is ever wasted. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear. The idea is simple: do the work fully, and let go of owning the result.
verse.for_you: You signed your first paying customer yesterday. That is a real win. But this verse tells you that the win is only the door. The real protection is in the doing, not the outcome. Keep your eye on the work itself, and let the result go.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verse.sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
verse.translation: The disciplined person, giving up the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined, attached to the fruit and driven by desire, is bound.
verse.why: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.
verse.misuse: Letting go of the payoff isn't refusing fair pay or recognition; it's not being chained to it.

prasang.title: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasang.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.
prasang.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that a person who gives up the fruit of action finds lasting peace. The one who stays attached to the result is bound. The disciplined person acts without being stained by the outcome, like a lotus leaf untouched by water. What comes next in the story is that this freedom is the mark of the wise.
verse.for_you: You signed the customer yesterday. That win is real. But the real test is the quiet month ahead when no one is watching. Let the result be what it is. Do the work without letting the high or the doubt take root.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from his text on steadfastness. He says the gods churned the ocean through jewels and poison until they found nectar. The verse tells us to let the worldly-wise blame or praise. Let fortune come or go as she pleases. Let death come today or ages hence. The steady do not move a step from the path of what is right. It asks you to stand firm on your own path while the noise of praise and blame passes by.
verse.for_you: You have signed your first customer after fourteen months. The praise is loud and the money is real, but it is just the door. The next year will ask if you can let the noise of praise and blame pass by and keep your feet on the path you chose.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi, the queen who was dragged into a hall of dice and lost everything, speaks to Yudhishthira, the eldest who is sitting in the forest after losing his kingdom. She sees him waiting for fate to fix things and she tells him that waiting is not a plan. She says that every attempt can end two ways, in success or not, and that the only way to be sure of failure is to do nothing at all.
verse.for_you: You signed the first customer yesterday. Now the quiet work begins. You are right to feel that the hard part starts now. This means you do not stop when the room is empty and the next order is not yet in sight.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.meaning: King Dhritarashtra cannot sleep the night before the peace talks. He calls his half-brother Vidura to his side. Vidura does not offer comfort. He says the wise person decides calmly and begins. They do not stop halfway, they do not waste time, and they keep themselves in hand. The king is being asked to choose a path and hold it, even when the ground feels uncertain.
verse.for_you: You signed the customer yesterday. Now the quiet work begins. Decide the one small task that moves the work forward, and hold to it without checking for praise.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verse.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
verse.line: So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.
verse.translation: Therefore, always do the work that has to be done, without attachment; by working without attachment a person reaches the highest.
verse.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on a battlefield, asking why the fulfilled would still act. He says even the wise, even God, work for the sake of the world, and the one content in the self has nothing left to gain. Yet the wise keep working, like Janaka, because others follow their example. The verse proposes that you could always do the work that needs doing, well and without clinging, and that is how you rise.
verse.for_you: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.

story.title: Building the bridge
story.story_hook: The army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey said he knew how to build a bridge.
story.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
story.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.
